note: Phrygian over a drone: the ♭2 a half step above home, the walk down from the 5th, then a made-up tune over i ♭II that lands on the ♭2 and steps home. The old Key choice is moves (key any, first in E) and its line opens with {{?key}}; the chords are tokens counted the long way.

exercise.title: Phrygian over a drone
exercise.why: Phrygian is set apart by the ♭2, a half step above home, and a half step that close to the drone shows at once when it is too wide, so the drone tells you how small to make it.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. The ringed note is {{b2}}, a half step above {{1}}. Sing {{1}}, {{b2}} and back to {{1}}, slowly. Sing it on "oo".
Then sing the whole Phrygian mode up from the low {{1}} and back down.
If {{b2}} comes out too high, sing {{1}} again and make the step smaller.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together. Sing down by step from {{5}} to {{1}}, and hold {{b2}} for a moment before you step home. Sing it on "ah".
Practice until the last step home lands without a slide.
{{?key}}In another key the drone moves, and the last step home is still a half step.
{{chord:i}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:bII}} is the chord built on {{b2}}, a half step up.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, playing {{chord:i}} and {{chord:bII}} in turn. Make up a short tune from the scale, and sing it on "la".
Land on {{b2}} when {{chord:bII}} comes round, and step down to {{1}} when {{chord:i}} comes back.
If you lose your place, hold {{1}} through both chords and start again.
